items.title: Can a crowd be better than the people in it? | Gustave Le Bon
items.description:
Think of the last time you were part of a crowd: a stadium, a protest, a packed train platform, a group chat that turned on someone.

Lessons and original commentary inspired by The Crowd by Gustave Le Bon. Modern exercises are our interpretations, not author quotations. Footage is illustrative, not historical or location evidence.

Chapters:
0:00 Two answers to one question
1:12 Why crowds get a bad name
2:18 The other side of the ledger
3:24 When self-interest switches off
4:29 Scoundrels with principles
5:33 What this does and does not prove
6:41 Reasoning is not always the hero

Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/445

items.title: Do you choose your face, or does it choose you? | Charles Darwin
items.description:
Do you choose your facial expressions, or do they choose you?

MindLore explains psychology from the original texts. Original commentary inspired by The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals by Charles Darwin. Modern examples are our interpretations, not author quotations.

Chapters:
0:00 Who controls your face?
1:06 Expression with a long history
2:07 Habit leaves movements behind
3:03 The dog and the principle of opposites
4:09 The blush and the watching mind
5:08 Does showing a feeling make it stronger?
6:10 Expressions as messages

Sources: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals by Charles Darwin (original text, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1227)

items.title: Why we notice so little of what is in front of us | William James
items.description:
Right now your eyes, ears, skin and inner body are sending a flood of signals, and you are aware of only a thin slice of it.

MindLore explains psychology from the original texts. Original commentary inspired by Psychology: Briefer Course by William James. Modern examples are our interpretations, not author quotations.

Chapters:
0:00 You miss almost everything
1:10 A tiny stream in a wide meadow
2:20 Why other thoughts wait outside
3:31 The fog we all fall into
4:39 Why meaning widens what you can take in
5:48 Can you really do two things at once?
7:03 The case of the busy emperor

Sources: Psychology: Briefer Course by William James (original text, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/55262)
